original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Answer #3683 OQ1 for present-head flag 0: on the published #2089 promote/add/restore at events 5758/5759/5807, census every window-named ADD source other than X0 as a non-self co-chart host alternative (FULL at ADD, FULL after restore, no post-channel destination, zero dirty-helper touches, zero endpoint repayment), retain uniqueness of X0 among registers named by ADD 5759 alone, and record the broader all-X co-chart count 103. Interpretive co-chart hosts on the published word only; no vector-equality claim and no dirty-helper construction.
scope_change_reason: #3683 OQ1 asks whether any non-self / copied-host alternative among event-named registers also achieves zero dirt-helper touches and zero endpoint repayment on this cut. #3683 already proved uniqueness among ADD-5759-named registers and left copied-host alternatives open. This package expands the search domain to window-named ADD sources (and all X registers) and certifies an affirmative co-chart census. Distinct from #3669 chronology, deferred flag0-head-span-schedule, and open #3532.
bottleneck_link: A legal I-G/2 completion needs an owner/host for every source read with dirty restoration. Showing many co-chart hosts with the same zero-dirt/zero-repay profile as S0 clarifies that self-ownership is not the only zero-mass interpretive host on this cut; priced dirty-helper copies remain the open mass question.
stop_rule: Stop after the 47-host window census and 103 all-X co-chart count are dual-scanned with dirt/repay checks. Do not build a dirty-helper copy word, reprint #3683 S0, reprint #3669 chronology, retarget #3532, or price a new kappa.
evidence: Window 5758..5807 has 48 Y34 adds whose first-seen sources are the listed 48 X-registers. Each of the 47 non-X0 sources holds FULL at 5759 and after 5807, has last destination inside the channel, and differs from its initial — so endpoint repay toward initials is false. Window dirty-helper touches = 0. ADD 5759 still names only {Y34,X0}, so S0 uniqueness on that ADD is unchanged. All 103 non-X0 X-registers match the same co-chart/zero-repay profile. Exemplar schedule S_cochart_X5. Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: What is the minimum added host rank mass for a dirty-helper copied-host word that routes the 5759 operand through a fresh helper while leaving X0/Y34 at channel finals?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Co-chart alternatives pay zero new host mass on the published word. A dirty-helper floor would price the gap between interpretive co-chart hosting and an actual copied operand.
open_questions.first_step: Search nested helper paths from empty to FULL that acquire a copy of the X0-valued read before 5759 and restore dirt after, with X0 unwritten in the window.
open_questions.blocked_by: No dirty-helper copied-host word is constructed here.

open_questions.question: Can a constructed dirt-restore program under S0 fit inside 5758–5807 without enlarging or replacing a published event?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The window is fully occupied by 2 transports and 48 adds with zero dirty-helper touches; a positive dirt-restore construction would need a free slot or a different cut.
open_questions.first_step: Attempt to insert a dirt-helper restore that preserves the published promote/add/restore semantics and remeasure dirt touches.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package only certifies the co-chart census; it does not construct or refute an inserted dirt-restore program.
